subject: reasoning
question:
E, F, G, H, K, L and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) .

N sits to the immediate right of E. Only three people sit between N and H when counted from the left of N. Only three people sit between E and K. F sits to the immediate right of G.

How many people sit between E and G when counted from the right of G?
solution:
**Given: **E, F, G, H, K, L and N are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) .

N sits to the immediate right of E. Only three people sit between N and H when counted from the left of N.

Only three people sit between E and K. F sits to the immediate right of G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7966fddbfb88ac05e5d55cf68b9c01822fb73d80a076e43b4e28aacf79de28c9.png] 

Thus, only one people sit between E and G when counted from the right of G.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**
